hong_lo: Hồng Lô Cốc, the furnace valley on the snowy north coast: clean, well-fitted robes of red-brown felt (rust to brick), with seal-skin boots, a seal-skin vest or coat and a collar of grey or white seal fur in the cold; forearms bare in the furnace hall and burn scars worn openly. Outer disciples wear plain rust-brown felt; inner disciples a deeper brick-red with a black cuff band; elders and the head dark red-brown with a white seal-fur collar. Boat crews wear glossy oiled seal-skin jackets over the felt. The Satchel Hall's healers wear a bright green leather satchel across the chest, the only green in the valley. Tools: bronze censers, copper snow jackets, cooling paddles, grey wool mittens. Plain but of good make, never ragged.
xuyen_lam: Xuyên Lâm Môn, the guides and staff fighters of the rain-forest road: clean, sturdy hemp tunics in forest-brown, olive and grey-green with crossed collars and woven rope or cloth belts; a straw rain cape over the shoulders (new gold straw for the young, silver-grey old straw for elders), straw-wrapped sandals or boots, and a bamboo staff worn pale at the grip. Outer disciples wear plain tan or brown hemp; inner disciples add a green sash; the head and elders wear heavier carrier's jackets and jade guide's tokens on cords. Tools: horn lanterns with bamboo-pith wicks, tally cords, bamboo knives. Plain and well made, never ragged.
ham_nguyet: Hàm Nguyệt Trang, the pearl-and-spirit-fish manor of the moon lake: divers wear grey sealskin and go barefoot on the piles; inner disciples wear clean undyed linen robes with a sash of the blue the lake turns in the evening; the mistress wears what she likes, with a pearl in each ear. Stewards and weighers add pale pearl-shell spectacles, pearl pins and strings of small pearls. Tools: oyster-shell lamps ground thin as paper, air-lines of waxed sea-silk, bone tweezers and brass pearl scales. Fine, clean and pale, never ragged.
thien_bao: Thiên Bảo Trai, the refiners-and-auction house of the western steppe: plain, perfectly pressed grey cloth, linen or silk, so that the goods on the table are the only colour in the room. A refiner wears a thin red-gold thread stitched round each cuff; an appraiser wears it at the collar edge; the mistress wears one red-gold pin and nothing else. Smiths add a leather apron or linked red-gold scale apron; clerks carry abacuses, scales, brass weights and brushes. Outer disciples wear plain grey with no thread. Cultivators dress well: crisp and clean, never ragged.
lanh_giang: Lãnh Giang Phái, the ice-hole sitters of the frozen Hàn Giang river: quilted fisher's robes in indigo-grey with crossed collars and toggles, a straw rain cape (pale gold, frost-white on the old) over the shoulders, and a wide straw hat in the old river shape tied with a blue cord, felt boots and thick leggings, all in the old Hàn Giang shape. Outer disciples wear short-sleeved quilted jackets and small capes; inner disciples full robes with blue cord trim; the head and elders heavy capes, frosted. Tools: ice chisels, bone fish-hooks on river-silk line, hemp tally cords, oars. Plain and warm, well made, never ragged.
